note: ArthaSaar Learning Hub — written in simple English. Educational only, not investment advice.

beginner: Learn first, earn later. Spend at least 1 month only studying before real money.
Start with a small SIP in a Nifty 50 index fund — it teaches you how markets move.
Do paper trading (fake trades) for 3 months. Write every trade in a notebook.
Buy only 1-2 stocks in the beginning. More stocks = more confusion.
NEVER touch futures & options as a beginner. 9 out of 10 beginners lose money in F&O.
Always keep a stop loss — even 1 trade without stop loss can destroy months of profit.
Don't buy stocks from WhatsApp/Telegram tips, YouTube 'sure shot' calls, or friends' friends.
Keep an emergency fund (6 months expenses) OUTSIDE the market.
Invest only that money which you will not need for 5 years.
On red days, don't panic sell. Markets fall and rise — that is normal breathing.
Read Zerodha Varsity free course — it is the best free education in India.
Track your trades: date, stock, buy price, reason, sell price, profit/loss, lesson learnt.
intermediate: Risk maximum 1-2% of your capital on one trade. With 1,00,000 capital, stop loss should be max 2,000.
Take trades only when reward is at least 2x the risk (1:2 risk-reward).
Learn position sizing: quantity = (capital x risk%) / (entry - stop loss).
Understand Open Interest (OI) and option chain before trading options.
Follow sector rotation — money moves from sector to sector. Strong sector = higher chance of win.
Don't trade every day. 3-4 good trades a month beat 30 random trades.
Backtest your strategy on past data before using real money.
Avoid expiry-day option buying — it is gambling with time value.
Review your trades every weekend: what worked, what failed, and why.
Know your taxes: short-term gains (< 1 year) are taxed higher than long-term.
advanced: Run 2-3 uncorrelated strategies so one bad month doesn't kill the year.
Size positions by volatility (ATR), not by fixed quantity — volatile stocks get smaller positions.
Control drawdown: if monthly loss crosses your limit (e.g. 8%), stop trading, review, restart next month.
Track your statistics: win rate, average win, average loss, biggest drawdown — improve the weakest number.
Trade the volatility regime — trends, ranges and event markets need different strategies.
Hedge before big events (Budget, RBI policy, elections) instead of guessing direction.
Allocate capital across timeframes: long-term core + short-term satellite + cash reserve.
Your edge is your journal — after 100+ logged trades, your mistakes will show you the money.

glossary.meaning: A small part of ownership in a company. If you own 1 share of a company with 100 shares, you own 1% of it.
National Stock Exchange and Bombay Stock Exchange — the two places in India where shares are bought and sold. NSE is bigger (Nifty), BSE is older (Sensex).
Securities and Exchange Board of India — the government referee of the market. Protects investors.
Your digital locker where shares are kept, like a bank account for stocks.
A basket of top companies showing overall market health. Nifty 50 = top 50 companies on NSE. Sensex = top 30 on BSE.
Initial Public Offering — when a company sells shares to the public for the first time to get listed on the exchange.
Grey Market Premium — unofficial price people pay before listing. High GMP usually means a strong listing, but it is not guaranteed.
Total value of a company = share price x total shares. Large cap = above ~1 lakh crore. Mid cap and small cap are smaller.
Price to Earnings. How many rupees you pay for 1 rupee of yearly profit. P/E 20 means you pay 20x yearly profit. Compare with similar companies, not across sectors.
Price to Book value — comparing market price with the company's net worth per share.
Return on Equity — profit made on shareholders' money. ROE above 15% for years usually means a good business.
Return on Capital Employed — profit on ALL capital (own + borrowed). The single best filter for business quality. Above 15% = strong.
Earnings Per Share — company profit divided by number of shares.
Company sharing profit with shareholders. Dividend yield = yearly dividend / price.
Face value is the original paper value of a share. Book value = what the company owns minus what it owes, per share.
The highest and lowest price in the last one year. Shows where the stock is in its yearly range.
Number of shares traded in a day. High volume = strong interest; moves without volume are suspect.
Exchange limit on daily price move (5%, 10%, 20%). In upper circuit there are only buyers, in lower circuit only sellers.
Bull = market going up with optimism. Bear = market falling with fear.
How fast prices swing. India VIX is the fear meter — VIX above 20 = fear, below 12 = calm.
Futures and Options — contracts to buy/sell at a fixed price on a future date. High leverage, high risk.
A contract to buy/sell at today's agreed price on a future date. You pay only margin, so profit and loss multiply.
A Call = right to BUY at strike price (profit when price rises). A Put = right to SELL (profit when price falls).
Strike = deal price. Premium = what you pay for the option. Expiry = last date (weekly on Thursday for Nifty/BankNifty).
In the money, at the money, out of the money — how close the option is to real profit. Far OTM options are lottery tickets.
Total contracts open in the market. Rising price + rising OI = strong trend. Falling OI = trend weakening.
F&O trades happen in fixed lots (e.g. Nifty 75). Margin = deposit you must keep with the broker.
Selling first hoping price falls, buying back cheaper. Profit in a falling market.
Mark to Market — daily profit/loss adjustment in your account while a trade is open.
Intraday = buy and sell same day. Delivery = shares come to your demat, keep as long as you want.
Swing = holding days to weeks. Positional = holding weeks to months.
Pre-fixed exit price to cut a losing trade. Your insurance policy — never trade without it.
Target = planned exit in profit. If risk is 10 points and target is 20, risk-reward is 1:2.
Support = price floor where buyers step in. Resistance = ceiling where sellers appear.
Price crossing a resistance with volume — often the start of a fast move.
Price moving sideways in a tight range — the market taking rest before the next big move.
General direction of price. Uptrend = higher highs and higher lows. Trade with the trend, not against it.
Exponential Moving Average — average price of last N days. Price above 200 EMA = long-term uptrend.
Relative Strength Index (0-100). Above 70 = overbought, below 30 = oversold, 40-70 = normal trend zone.
A bar showing open, high, low, close. Green = closed up, red = closed down. Patterns tell trader mood.
Foreign and Domestic Institutional Investors — the big money. Their daily buying/selling moves the market.
Bonus = extra free shares. Split = one share divided into many. Price adjusts; your value stays same.
Company buying its own shares — usually a sign of confidence and reduces share count.
Company offering existing shareholders new shares at a discount to raise money.
Shares available for public trading. High liquidity = easy to buy/sell without moving price.
Difference between expected and actual trade price — cost of fast markets or illiquid stocks.
Average True Range — how much a stock moves daily on average. Used for stop loss distance.
Deciding HOW MANY shares to buy based on your stop loss and risk limit. Formula: qty = (capital x risk%) / (entry − stop loss).
Earning returns on returns. 1 lakh at 15% a year becomes ~4 lakh in 10 years, ~16 lakh in 20 years. Time is the fuel.
Stock hitting circuit limits repeatedly can enter F&O ban — trading in its futures stops for some days.

rules.rule: Never risk more than 1-2% of capital on one trade
rules.why: One bad trade should never become one bad month.

rules.rule: Stop loss is compulsory, not optional
rules.why: A small planned loss is a business cost; a big unplanned loss is a disaster.
Adding to a falling stock doubles your mistake. Average winners, never losers.

rules.rule: Book partial profits when a stock doubles
rules.why: Sell half — the rest runs free of cost. Your capital is safe, hope rides free.
Entry, stop loss, target, quantity — decided when calm, not when emotional.

rules.rule: No revenge trading after a loss
rules.why: Trying to 'win it back today' is how one loss becomes five.
Uptrends, downtrends and ranges need different trades. Fighting the trend is expensive.
More positions = divided attention = missed stop losses.
Waiting with cash is a strategy. You don't have to trade every day.
Interest + pressure + leverage = account killer. Only trade your own spare money.

rules.rule: Avoid tips, follow your own system
rules.why: If you don't know WHY you bought, you won't know WHEN to sell.

rules.rule: Write a journal for every single trade
rules.why: After 100 trades your journal is worth more than any course.
Enter last, exit first — decide both ends of the trade in advance.
Master one setup over 50+ trades before adding another.
Missed money is not lost money. There is no FOMO in a career of decades.

rules.rule: Never trade on expiry day with options buying
rules.why: Time value dies fastest on expiry day — odds are worst.

rules.rule: Protect capital first, profits come later
rules.why: You can recover lost time, not lost capital. Defence wins compounding.
Anger, euphoria, fear — all three drain accounts. Trade only when calm.
First headline is often wrong. Fake news moves prices for 10 minutes.
Weekly review of trades catches mistakes while they are small.

rules.rule: Diversify across sectors, not just stocks
rules.why: 5 banking stocks = 1 bet on banking. Spread across sectors.

rules.rule: Doubles don't come from doubling risk
rules.why: Slow is smooth, smooth is fast. Compounding hates big drawdowns.

psychology.point: When you feel 'everyone is making money except me', that is exactly when you will buy tops. The market rewards patience, not speed.
Greed makes you hold past your target, skip stop losses, and over-size positions. Greed turns winners into losers more often than bad analysis.
Hope is good in life, poison in trading. 'It will come back up' has destroyed more accounts than any crash. The market doesn't know your price.
After a loss, the urge to immediately win it back with a bigger trade feels logical — it is not. The market doesn't owe you anything. Take the loss, take a walk, come back tomorrow.
A mediocre strategy followed strictly beats a brilliant strategy followed emotionally. Your edge is not IQ — it is repetition without deviation.
A good trade can lose money; a bad trade can win money. Judge yourself on whether you followed your rules, not on the day's P&L.
Shopkeepers accept shop rent; traders accept small planned losses. Your stop loss IS the rent of the trading business.
Most bad trades come not from fear or greed but from boredom — 'let me just do something'. Sitting still is a skill.
When you feel invincible after a streak of wins, that is the most dangerous moment. Big losses follow big wins — size down after a winning streak.
Your best long-term buys will always feel terrifying. The news will be worst exactly when prices are best. Fear is the price of the bargain.
After a bull run everyone becomes a genius — until the trend changes. In a rising market, a monkey throwing darts also makes money. Respect the cycle.
Someone will always make more, faster. Their risk appetite, capital and luck are not yours. The only comparison that matters: are you better than last year?
Retail traders' only real advantages over institutions are time and no pressure. Use them — wait for YOUR setup, not any setup.
Next to every trade, write how you felt. Over months you will see which emotion costs you the most money — then guard against it.
Trading is probability, not prediction. You don't need to be right — you need to make more when right than you lose when wrong.

intraday.name: Opening Range Breakout (ORB)
intraday.how: Mark the high and low of the first 15 minutes (9:15-9:30). Buy if price breaks the high with volume; sell/short on break of low.
intraday.when: Trending days, after a quiet previous close.
intraday.risk: False breakouts are common — stop loss on the other side of the range.

intraday.name: VWAP Pullback
intraday.how: In an uptrend day, when price pulls back to the VWAP line (average price of the day) and holds, buy with stop below VWAP.
intraday.when: Strong trend days where Nifty is clearly one-directional.
intraday.risk: Choppy days give repeated small losses.

intraday.name: Index-Sync Trading
intraday.how: Only trade stock in the SAME direction as Nifty/BankNifty at that moment. Nifty red = only sell-side candidates; Nifty green = only buy-side.
intraday.when: Every day — it is a filter more than a strategy.
intraday.risk: None extra — it simply removes fights against the tide.

intraday.name: Gap-and-Go (Momentum)
intraday.how: Stocks that gap up 2-4% on news and keep rising with huge volume in the first 30 minutes often continue. Enter on the first small pullback.
intraday.risk: News fades fast — strict stop and quick exits needed.

intraday.name: Last-Hour Trend
intraday.how: 3:00-3:30 PM, if Nifty shows a clear direction with volume, index or large-cap moves often continue to close. Enter small with stop loss.
intraday.when: Days with conviction into the last hour.
intraday.risk: Sudden reversals in the final 15 minutes.

short_term.name: Breakout with Volume
short_term.how: Stock consolidating 2-6 weeks in a tight range, then closes above range top with 2x+ volume. Buy on breakout or first retest.
short_term.risk: Failed breakouts — stop loss just inside the range.

short_term.name: 20-EMA Pullback in Uptrend
short_term.how: Stock above 20 and 50 EMA, rising steadily. Buy when it pulls back to the 20 EMA and shows a green candle. Stop below 50 EMA.
short_term.when: Healthy uptrends after a strong run.
short_term.risk: Deep corrections — exit if 50 EMA breaks.

short_term.name: Support Bounce
short_term.how: Stock repeatedly taking support at the same level (2+ touches) and turning up with volume. Buy at support, stop just below it.
short_term.risk: Third or fourth touch often breaks — take the first bounce only.

short_term.name: Relative Strength vs Nifty
short_term.how: Compare the stock with Nifty over 3 months. Stock falling less in a fall, rising more in a rise = strong. Trade only the strongest 10.
short_term.when: Always — best filter in the ArthaSaar screener.

long_term.name: Quality Compounders
long_term.how: Buy companies with ROCE above 15% for 5+ years, low debt, honest promoters, growing profits. Hold 5-10 years, add on falls.
long_term.when: Any time — you are buying businesses, not prices.
long_term.risk: Business quality falling — review results every quarter (ArthaSaar Deep Fund tab helps).

long_term.name: Reasonable Price for Quality
long_term.how: Even a great company is a bad stock at a crazy price. Wait for P/E below the stock's own 5-year average, or market crashes.
long_term.when: Corrections and bear markets — when others are scared.
long_term.risk: Great companies rarely become cheap — patience needed.

long_term.name: Sector Tailwind Investing
long_term.how: Pick a sector with a 5-10 year growth story (e.g. defence, power, electronics) and buy 2-3 quality leaders of that sector.
long_term.when: Early in the sector cycle, not after it has doubled.
long_term.risk: Sector story dying — policy change, technology shift.

long_term.name: Staggered Buying (SIP for stocks)
long_term.how: Never invest all at once. Divide into 6-12 parts, buy monthly or on every 5% fall. Removes timing tension.

long_term.name: Thesis Checking (when to sell)
long_term.how: Write down WHY you bought. Sell only if: (1) thesis broken (2) management issues (3) you found clearly better. NOT because price fell.
long_term.risk: Emotional selling without reason — the journal prevents it.

options.name: Buying Calls on Breakouts
options.how: Buy slightly ITM calls only when the underlying gives a confirmed breakout with volume. Stop loss on option premium or on spot breaking the level.
options.when: Strong trending markets with clear technical setups.
options.risk: TIME VALUE — even if direction is right, slow moves kill option buyers. Use monthly contracts for slower moves.

options.name: Buying Puts on Breakdowns
options.how: Mirror image: buy puts on confirmed support breakdowns in a weak market.
options.risk: VIX falling after entry shrinks premium — fast moves needed.

options.name: Covered Call (income)
options.how: If you own 75+ shares of a stock, sell one slightly OTM call against it each month. You keep the premium if the stock stays below strike.
options.risk: You cap your upside if the stock rockets. Still keep the shares either way.

options.name: Hedging with Puts
options.how: Before big events (Budget, elections, RBI), buy protective puts on your portfolio or Nifty. It is insurance — a small known cost to avoid disaster.
options.when: When holding large positions through risky events.
options.risk: Insurance expires worthless in calm markets — that is the cost of peace of mind.

options.name: AVOID: Weekly OTM Lottery
options.how: Buying far OTM weekly options because they are cheap is buying lottery tickets. Cheap for a reason — they mostly expire zero.
options.when: Never. If someone explains it as 'small investment, big return' — that is the trap.
options.risk: Near-certain slow account death. The option seller is your casino house.

options.name: Credit Spreads (Advanced)
options.how: Sell an OTM option and buy a further OTM option (same type). You collect the difference and both sides are capped. Works when you expect a range.
options.when: Range-bound markets, with full margin understanding.
options.risk: Margin blocked is large; a big move against you hurts. Learn deeply before trying.

futures.name: Trend Following with Index Futures
futures.how: Trade NIFTY futures in the direction of the daily trend with a stop loss. One lot, small size, strict stops.
futures.risk: Leverage cuts both ways — a 2% Nifty move = 100% of one lot margin on edge. Respect size.

futures.name: Rollover + OI Watching
futures.how: Near expiry, watch rollover % and OI building in next month contracts. High rollover = trend expects to continue.
futures.when: Expiry week (last Tuesday-Wednesday of the month).
futures.risk: Rollover data is a hint, not a promise.

futures.name: Cash-Futures Basis
futures.how: When futures trade far above spot (high premium), institutions are greedy; far below (discount) = fear. Basis normalising often signals direction change.
futures.when: Reading market mood — ArthaSaar Futures tab shows basis for 80 stocks.
futures.risk: Interpretation tool, not a standalone signal.

futures.name: Portfolio Hedge with Futures
futures.how: If holding a large stock portfolio and expecting a fall, short NIFTY futures of equal value instead of selling shares (saves taxes and costs).
futures.risk: If market rises instead, hedge loses while portfolio gains — a net wash, that is the design.

intraday_checklist: Liquidity: average volume high — you can enter and exit instantly.
Movement: stock should have decent daily range (check ATR). Dead stock = dead trade.
In sync: same direction as Nifty/BankNifty at that moment (Index-Sync rule).
News/results known: know WHY it is moving today.
Clear levels: visible support/resistance for entry and stop loss.
Volume confirmation: moves backed by volume, not thin air.
Avoid: expiry-day chaos, F&O ban stocks, IPO listing week stocks.
Position size: calculated from stop loss, not gut feeling.
Time: best windows 9:15-10:30 and 2:45-3:30. Avoid sleepy noon.
One shot rule: 2-3 quality attempts a day maximum. More = donating.
short_term_checklist: Trend: price above 20 and 50 EMA (screener filter: Above EMA200).
Momentum: RSI between 50 and 70 — strong but not overbought.
Volume: recent up-days with higher volume than down-days.
Setup: near breakout of consolidation OR pullback to support in uptrend.
Sector: the stock's sector is strong vs Nifty (relative strength).
Market: Nifty itself is stable or rising. No trades in falling-knife markets.
Risk-reward: minimum 1:2 from entry to target vs stop loss.
Size small: swing positions max 5-10% capital each.
Stop loss: below the swing low / support that justified the entry.
Horizon: 2-6 weeks planned. Set a review reminder.
long_term_checklist: ROCE above 15% consistently for 5+ years (Deep Fund tab).
Profit growing: Sales and net profit growing every year (quarterly YoY in Deep Fund).
Promoters: high holding, LOW or zero pledge, no frequent selling (Deep Fund tab).
Free cash: company generates cash, not just paper profit.
Sector runway: business relevant for the next 10 years.
Valuation sane: P/E not far above its own 5-year average; compare with peers.
Management honest: clean accounts, no SEBI cases, shareholder-friendly history.
Buy in parts: staggered entries over months, add on market falls.
Review quarterly: read results (ArthaSaar files them to Notion automatically) — sell only if thesis breaks, never on price falls alone.
Portfolio: 8-12 stocks across 5+ sectors. More is diworsification.
Hold through noise: crashes are entry points, not exit points — IF the checklist still passes.

quick_tips: The market transfers money from the impatient to the patient.
Your first job is not making profit — it is surviving long enough to get good.
Red day + good stock = discount sale for long-term buyers.
If you cannot explain the trade in one line, do not take it.
Stop loss is your employee — do not fire it.
Simplicity survives; complexity dies in stress.
The best traders do nothing most days — and everything on their one day.
Bull markets make everyone a genius; risk management makes you a survivor.
